chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It suffices you in the Qunut (supplication) to say: 'O Allah, forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.' Indeed, You are Able to do all things.

And the Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned in the book that he raises his hands for the Qunut without the Takbir, and the preferable view in my opinion is that he raises them with the Takbir, and that which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended text for Qunut in Shia prayer and how should hands be raised?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific supplicatory formula for Qunut, emphasizing divine attributes of mercy and omnipotence, while also addressing the fiqh of hand elevation. It highlights the scholarly nuance between raising hands with or without the Takbir, reflecting the practical application of Imami jurisprudence in ritual prayer. The text underscores the importance of both the verbal content of the dua and the physical etiquette (adab) of the worshipper during this specific moment of supplication.
